contentChunks.htmlValue: Availability & resources
M3 Expressive update

May 2025

The extended FAB now has three sizes: small, medium, and large, each with updated type styles. These align with the FAB sizes for an easier transition between FABs. The baseline extended FAB is no longer recommended and should be replaced with the small extended FAB. Surface and FABs are also no longer recommended. More on M3 Expressive

Variants and naming:

  • Added new sizes

    • Small: 56dp

    • Medium: 80dp

    • Large: 96dp

  • No longer recommended

    • Baseline extended FAB (56dp)

    • Surface extended FAB

Updates:

  • Adjusted typography to be larger

contentChunks.htmlValue: Color

Color values are implemented through design tokens. For design, this means working with color values that correspond with tokens. For implementation, a color value will be a token that references a value. Learn more about design tokens

Color styles

Extended FABs can use several combinations of color and on color styles, such as primary and on primary. The following color mappings provide the same level of contrast and functionality, so choose a color mapping based on visual preference.

contentChunks.footer:
Extended FAB color roles used for light and dark schemes:

  1. Primary container & on primary container (default)
  2. Secondary container & on secondary container
  3. Tertiary container & on tertiary container
  4. Primary & on primary
  5. Secondary & on secondary
  6. Tertiary & on tertiary
contentChunks.altText: 6 extended FAB color styles.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Use an extended FAB on screens with long, scrolling views that require persistent access to an action, such as a checkout screen. 

Use it when label text helps understand the main action, or to add further emphasis to the button.

contentChunks.footer: Extended FABs ensure the main action is visible at all times
contentChunks.altText: A centered extended FAB is used to check out in a shopping app.

contentChunks.footer: Use an extended FAB to provide constant access to a primary action above long-scrolling surface content
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB on an article with lots of body content to publish that article.

contentChunks.footer: Use an extended FAB to emphasize a page’s primary action
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB on a task list to create a new task.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Additional emphasis

The extended FAB can provide more emphasis and clarity to a product’s primary action. 

Since it has room for both a text label and icon, the extended FAB can be effective where an icon alone is ambiguous. However, the relationship between an extended FAB's icon and label should be clear.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB can be effective where an icon alone is too vague
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB labeled “find flights” with an airplane icon, which would be unclear on its own.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Like the regular FAB, only one extended FAB should be used per screen. 

Multiple FABs compete for attention. 

If additional high-level actions are required, consider adding more buttons elsewhere on the page.

contentChunks.footer: Only show one prominent action at a time with the extended FAB
contentChunks.altText: An extended FAB used on a screen.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use multiple extended FABs in one screen as it disrupts visual hierarchy
contentChunks.altText: 2 extended FABs used on 1 screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
The extended FAB shouldn't be used as an option in a set of actions. 

Instead, use filled buttons for a similar level of emphasis.

contentChunks.footer: Use a button with appropriate styling to emphasize it in a group of buttons
contentChunks.altText: Filled button labeled “finish setup” next to a “back” button.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use the extended FAB to convey an option in a set of actions
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB labeled “finish setup” next to a “back” button.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Choosing a size

There are three variants of extended FABs: small, medium, and large.

Choose an appropriately-sized extended FAB to add the right amount of emphasis for an action. 

In compact windows with one prominent action, the large extended FAB can be appropriate.

In larger breakpoints, use a medium or large extended FAB.

contentChunks.footer: There are three sizes of extended FABs
contentChunks.altText: 1 large, 1 medium, and 1 small extended FAB on 3 different screen sizes.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Container

The extended FAB container is a rounded rectangle that hugs its contents. 

The extended FAB grows and shrinks with text length.

contentChunks.footer: The extended FAB container hugs the icon and text
contentChunks.altText: Fixed-width extended FAB, centered, ignoring layout grid.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Icon (optional)

An extended FAB's icon should intuitively represent its action.

contentChunks.footer: Unlike standard FABs, extended FABs don't require an icon
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB without an icon, labeled “Save draft”.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB can't have an icon without a text label
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB with icon only, with no label text.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Label text

The extended FAB’s label should clearly describe its action.

Use 1–2 words at most. Keep in mind that localization may increase the amount of characters and width of the extended FAB.

contentChunks.footer: Shorten the text as much as needed. Include an icon for additional context.
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB with short text “Save”.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid wrapping or truncating text
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB with wrapping text “Save draft in folder”.

contentChunks.footer: Place the extended FAB above the rest of the UI, off of elements like app bars
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB placed above navigation bar.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t place the extended FAB on top of toolbars. It disrupts the consistency of the elevation and surface layers.
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB overlaid on a docked toolbar.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t place the extended FAB in the upper half of a mobile screen, as it disrupts the reading of the UI
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB below an app bar at the top of a mobile screen.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t place extended FABs on cards or inside other containers
contentChunks.altText: An extended FAB labeled "Confirm" on a dialog to "Confirm your location".

contentChunks.htmlValue: Avoid putting other floating components, like the floating toolbar, on screen with the extended FAB.

contentChunks.altText: The extended FAB is next to a floating toolbar.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Responsive layout

The FAB and extended FAB can transform into each other depending on available space and layout. 

In a collapsed navigation rail, a FAB would be used. When the rail is expanded, the FAB can transform into an extended FAB.

contentChunks.footer: When space is limited, an extended FAB can transform into a FAB
contentChunks.altText: Example of extended FAB transforming into standard FAB.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Right-to-left languages

Extended FABs should mirror their elements in right-to-left (RTL) languages.

contentChunks.footer: Icons should be placed to the left of labels for left-to-right (LTR) languages
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB in a left-to-right language placed at the bottom right of a screen. The icon is to the left of the text.

contentChunks.footer: Icons should be placed to the right of labels for RTL languages
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB in a right-to-left language placed at the bottom left of a screen. The icon is to the right of the text.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Breakpoints

In compact and medium breakpoints, the extended FAB should be placed at the bottom of the screen, either center-aligned or aligned to the trailing edge of the window.

contentChunks.footer: The extended FAB can be center-aligned
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB center-aligned on a mobile screen.

contentChunks.footer: The extended FAB can be aligned to the trailing edge of the window
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB right-aligned on a mobile screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
In expanded and larger breakpoints, the extended FAB should appear either:

  • At the bottom right edge of the window, in both LTR and RTL languages

  • Within the navigation rail

contentChunks.footer: The extended FAB can be right-aligned in both LTR and RTL languages
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB at bottom right of screen.

contentChunks.footer: The extended FAB can be at the top of the expanded navigation rail
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB in navigation drawer.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior

Appearing

The extended FAB surface expands when appearing on screen using an enter and exit transition pattern.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB expands when appearing on screen
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB appearing on screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Expanding

The extended FAB can expand and adapt to any shape using a container transform transition pattern. 

This includes a surface that is part of the app structure, or a surface that spans the entire screen.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB can expand and adapt to any shape
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB adapting to various shapes.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Transforming

The extended FAB can transform into a FAB on scroll to temporarily take up less space on screen.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB can transform into a FAB
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB transforming into a FAB when the page is scrolled.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Scrolling

The extended FAB can transform into a FAB when scrolling down, and back to an extended FAB when scrolling up.

contentChunks.footer: An extended FAB collapses and expands when scrolling
contentChunks.altText: Extended FAB transforming while scrolling.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
When the FAB switches to an extended FAB, the following transitions occur:

  • The FAB shape changes
  • FAB icon moves to the left
  • FAB text label fades in

contentChunks.footer: FAB switches to an extended FAB
contentChunks.altText: FAB transforming into extended FAB.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Use cases

People should be able to do the following using assistive technology:

  • Navigate to and activate the extended FAB
Interaction & style

To make it easier for users of screen readers to reach a primary action such as an extended FAB, consider placing the action in the upper left region of large web screens, like in an expanded navigation rail.

In smaller windows, the best place for the extended FAB is the lower right corner of a screen.

contentChunks.footer: Extended FABs can be placed in the expanded navigation rail
contentChunks.altText: On a large screen, the Compose FAB is placed on the upper left region in an email app with the expanded window on the right.

contentChunks.footer: Place extended FABs in an easy-to-reach place that doesn’t obstruct other actions
contentChunks.altText: In a compact window, the Compose FAB is placed on the lower right region in an email app.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t place extended FABs over another actionable element
contentChunks.altText: In a compact window, the Compose FAB is overlapping other buttons in an email app.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Initial focus

Ensure the extended FAB is prioritized in the overall focus order to create an efficient experience for people who navigate UIs with assistive tech. 

On mobile, the focus order may start with the app bar, move to the navigation bar, and then skip past any other content on the page to land on the extended FAB.

When using an extended FAB, both the visible label and icon should be treated as one focusable element. The extended FAB doesn’t need a tooltip because it already has a visible label.

contentChunks.footer: Ensure extended FABs get focus when navigating with assistive technology
contentChunks.altText: A focused extended FAB in the lower right region of a mobile screen.

contentChunks.footer: Tooltips aren’t required since the extended FAB has label text
contentChunks.altText: A focused extended FAB with a tooltip matching the text label.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

Keys
Actions
TabMoves focus to the extended FAB
Space or Enter
Activates the extended FAB
Labeling elements

To ensure the action is clear, use consistent icons and text labels, such as a Compose icon with a Compose text label. 

The icon and text label combination should have one distinct purpose.

The accessibility label must include the same first word as the visible label. For example, if the visible button is Create, then the accessibility label might say Create a new invite.

contentChunks.footer: The accessibility label reads Compose to match the extended FAB's displayed label
contentChunks.altText: Accessibility labels of an extended FAB.
